title: Studio Reel storyboard
description: The authoring IR for films/<film>/storyboard.json. This file exists because IGNORED_BY_EMITTER is a hand-maintained LIST, so a field the author INVENTED is indistinguishable from a field the design deliberately does not express. jan-suraaj's `label_bg` is the case that justifies it: the emitter's field is `slab_bg`, the name was dropped, and for the last five seconds of the film the call to action rendered near-black on near-black at 1.05:1 with a green build. `additionalProperties: false` turns that class of mistake into a build error with a JSON pointer. Fields are marked APPLIED or DISCARDED; a DISCARDED field is accepted and reported by reel-compile.cjs, which is the honest outcome — it is deliberate, not accidental.

note.description: Author annotation. Never compiled; never reported.

hexOrToken.description: A literal `#rgb`/`#rrggbb`/`#rrggbbaa`, or the NAME of a key in this film's design.tokens. Resolved by reel-compile.cjs; an unresolvable name is a warning that names the fallback it used.

tokenTable.description: A film's own palette. Keyed by whatever the brand calls its colours — `coal`, `container`, `tertiary` — which is exactly why no code may infer a role from a name.

surface.description: APPLIED. A scene or reel background. `type` names a recipe the compiler implements; an unknown type is reported rather than flattened to a colour nobody asked for.

type.description: flat = `base` only; dots/blueprint = a repeating pattern over `base`; gradient = two stops from/angle; linear-gradient/radial-gradient = `value` passed through verbatim as the gradient body.

ink.description: Pattern colour (the dot, or the blueprint line).

value.description: The whole gradient body for linear-gradient/radial-gradient. Rejected if it contains ; { } < >.

typeStep.description: APPLIED (via resolveRamp). One step of `frame.ramp`, in 1920x1080 design-space px — not vw. The emitter turns `size` into a stage-relative vw length so a clip survives any stage size; `type_scale.min_px` adds a legibility floor underneath it.

fontRole.description: APPLIED — `family` reaches the clip as a real webfont <link>. `usage` and `script` are author notes.

themeRole.description: A role the emitter paints, pointing at THIS film's token name. Naming a role the emitter has no key for is a build failure, not a silent drop — that is the rule that stops a plausible default standing in for a declaration.

fill.description: A FILLED component's surface — container / primary-container.

fill-ink.description: The type drawn on a filled component. A different role from `ink`: a bright block carries dark type, a dark stage carries light type.

fill-tone.description: The TONAL component surface. Unset, the emitter mixes the ink at 14% over the stage.

on-variant.description: The muted secondary ink the chart CSS reads for axis labels, ticks and legends. A variable the stylesheet consumes and the theme cannot set is a hardcoded colour wearing a var() costume.

chart-grid.description: Gridlines and axis rules. Themed for the same reason the meter track is: a grid hardcoded to rgba(255,255,255,.13) is invisible on a light stage and reads as "no grid authored" rather than "grid I cannot see".

mode.description: One runtime theme. `tokens` is MERGED over the base table rather than replacing it, so a mode only names what differs. Every declared mode ships in the SAME clip as a [data-mode] rule, which is what lets one artefact serve both a light and a dark viewer.

typeScale.description: APPLIED. A whole type system in one block instead of nine hand-tuned ramp steps. `preset` is a FLOOR: frame.ramp still wins, so an existing film can adopt a preset and keep its own numbers. `scale` multiplies the ramp; `min_px` is a legibility floor for embeds narrower than the design space. reel-compile.cjs asserts the ramp is monotonic, because a scale change can otherwise invert the hierarchy silently.

radii.description: APPLIED. One radius per component. Material uses 8 on a chip, 20 on a card and 24 on its answer block in ONE screen, which a single --hss-radius cannot carry — so a film had to pick one number and live with it on all four. Anything not named falls back to design.radius.

fills.description: APPLIED. The variant each component type defaults to, stated ONCE per film instead of on every element. Elements override with their own `fill`.

fillName.description: filled = the theme's container surface with on-container ink; tonal = the low-emphasis container; outlined = border only; text = bare. Anything outside this set fails the build rather than rendering the element without its variant.

textWidth.description: APPLIED. The prose measure, expressed ONCE per role (Material's max-width:44rem) instead of repeated on every paragraph. An element's own max_width still wins.

design.description: The design system. Everything here that has no mapping is reported by reel-compile.cjs; anything whose NAME is not in this schema is a build failure.

style.description: DISCARDED, informational. Names the style LANGUAGE ("material 3", "neo-brutalism"). Not actionable on its own — the actionable half is `fills` + `radii`, which say which treatments and which shapes that language means. Stating this alone prints one informational line naming the per-element `fill` vocabulary.

modes.description: Runtime themes compiled into the SAME clip as [data-mode] rules. A design that ships two themes is one artefact, not two files to keep in step.

hover.description: DISCARDED, informational. A video has no hover. Kept so the design record stays complete; it is reported beside IGNORED_BY_EMITTER rather than as a failure, because a red you cannot fix trains you to ignore the red.

src.description: APPLIED-gated. Where the KaTeX renderer comes from. DEFAULTS TO `vendor/katex` — the dist vendored at public/vendor/katex, which is INLINED into the clip (one <style> with every face as a woff2 data URI, plus two data: URL scripts) so the clip renders with no network at all: exported to a bare file, opened from file://, read on a plane. EMPTY is a hard failure for a film with latex elements, because that is exactly what an offline export produces: raw `$$…$$` with no error and a green gate. A `cdn:` value is reported as informational, not failed — the compiler cannot prove the network works — and ships the three jsDelivr tags instead. Only `latex` triggers any of this: `answer` is plain text with no delimiters.

frame.description: The design space. `design_space` and `safe` are DISCARDED — the emitter is stage-relative and takes its geometry from the stage it is embedded in. `ramp` is APPLIED and wins over any type_scale preset.

safe.description: DISCARDED. Authored for a designer; there is no safe-area layer to apply it to.

beat.description: DISCARDED. Authored pacing intent in seconds.

ramp.description: APPLIED. Role name -> step. Role names are the film's own; the compiler resolves each through type_scale and then asserts the ORDER is monotonic.

entrance.description: APPLIED except `ease` and `type: slot`. The runtime hardcodes three curves (ease-out, back, else fade), so every authored cubic-bezier is discarded and reported; `slot` falls through to the fade branch and loses `from_scale`. `draw` is the shape mark's own entrance: the host holds still at full opacity while the stroke or wipe carries the phase, so the mark draws itself on its own timing — on a non-shape it pins visible with no motion, which makes it a shape-only entrance rather than a broken one. Animations are a pure function of t — never a wall clock and never a CSS transition — or scrub, deep links and the exporter disagree with each other.

chartSegment.description: APPLIED for chart (donut). One ring segment, index-aligned with series[0]. Separate from $defs/item because a pie is the one chart where the colour is a FIXED categorical slot and the ORDER carries the meaning — reusing `accent` would have made the donut's palette read like an item's highlight.

chartSeries.description: APPLIED for chart. One series: a name for the legend and one value per category. `color` is a hex or a TOKEN in the film's own palette, resolved against the mode in force — so a series named as a token swaps with the theme instead of being the one hand-picked colour of the five that does not.

item.description: APPLIED for the element types that have items: pills (a string), tiles (icon/head/body), cards (label/accent/muted). One shape covering all three.

element.description: One element. The property list is the UNION across all types rather than a per-type oneOf: the field NAME is what this schema exists to police, and a typo is the failure mode that shipped (`label_bg` for `slab_bg`). Each property below says whether it is APPLIED or DISCARDED.

type.description: Anything else is a HARD FAILURE at the emitter: buildElHtml throws, and reel-compile reports the element as deferred with the emitter's own message. It used to fall out of the switch and emit an EMPTY <div class="hss-el"> with no warning — the exact silent failure this pipeline was built to remove, and the reason the emitter now has a throwing `default`. This enum is a convenience for the authoring side only; the emitter's switch is the contract.

at_ms.description: APPLIED — offset from the scene start.

text.description: APPLIED for text/latex/answer/credit. latex and answer are spliced UNESCAPED so backslashes and bare `&` alignment markers survive, so an angle bracket in one of those is a hard failure, not a warning.

value.description: APPLIED for stat. The numeral; its gradient is one authored colour plus a CSS stop.

label.description: APPLIED for stat. The caption under the numeral.

chart.description: APPLIED for chart. `columns` and `bars` are the same marks on the other axis; `line` carries the optional `area` fill; `donut` reads series[0] as its segments. Geometry is computed once at compile time and is animated from t, so a chart scrubs like the rest of the film.

series.description: APPLIED for chart. One entry per colour; every series is drawn.

categories.description: APPLIED for chart. The axis labels, one per value. Shorter than the data it is padded, not truncated.

stacked.description: APPLIED for chart (columns/bars). The scale SUMS the column before asking for the max — reading a single series would clip the stack.

area.description: APPLIED for chart (line). Fills under the line, revealed left-to-right by an animated clip so the fill and the stroke arrive together.

values.description: APPLIED for chart. Value labels on the marks; off for line, whose labels would collide with the stroke.

grid.description: APPLIED for chart (default true). Gridlines and axis ticks.

legend.description: APPLIED for chart (default true when more than one series).

min.description: APPLIED for chart. The axis floor. Unauthored, or 0, means the axis starts at 0 — and that default is the editorial rule this used to be instead of an option: a truncated axis is a lie the reader cannot see, so nothing could accidentally be truncated. An authored floor ABOVE 0 is applied and REPORTED by reel-compile as a declared choice, because a threshold film needs it: times that move 18 seconds inside a 241-second space draw as a flat line from 0, and the barrier the film is about disappears into it. Ignored for `stacked`, where every layer would be shrunk by the same offset and the stack would stop summing to its own column.

max.description: APPLIED for chart. An authored ceiling, so two charts on one screen share an axis; otherwise the data sets the scale.

ref.description: APPLIED for chart (columns/bars/line). A threshold drawn across the plot at this value — the record that stood, the limit, the target. Horizontal on columns/line, VERTICAL on bars, for the same reason the grid is: on bars the value axis runs left to right, and a horizontal rule behind the bars reads as another bar. Drawn even when `grid` is off, because a threshold is usually the point of the chart. It never clamps the axis: a threshold above the data sits outside the plot rather than inflating the scale to hide the gap, and the coordinate is clamped to the plot rect so the line stays on the graphic.

ref_label.description: APPLIED for chart (with `ref`). The words beside the line. Defaults to the formatted value plus the unit — authored when the number has a name the film would rather say: 4:00.00 rather than 240.

unit.description: APPLIED for chart. Appended to the top axis tick and the foot.

decimals.description: APPLIED for chart. Decimal places on every printed number.

kicker.description: APPLIED for chart. The eyebrow above the title — how an editorial graphic says which section it belongs to.

title.description: APPLIED for chart. Authored INSIDE the element rather than as a sibling text element, so the graphic and its headline cannot drift apart or be reordered.

source.description: APPLIED for chart. The provenance line. A number without its source is the thing a data story exists to fix.

chart_at_ms.description: APPLIED for chart — the mark-drawing phase offset from the element's own at_ms, so a title can settle while the bars are still growing.

chart_in.description: APPLIED for chart — the mark-drawing phase. `stagger_ms` here is the per-bar delay, which is the whole difference between a chart and a block that changes size.

role.description: APPLIED (indirectly) — resolves through frame.ramp or type_scale for SIZE and WEIGHT, and through design.fonts for the family. `role` is how a text element says which step of the type system it is; it is the answer to "how do I change text size" without touching any element.

style.description: DISCARDED, advisory. Names the component ("slab", "label", "display") so a reader can tell what a scene is made of. It is NOT the visual switch — that is `fill`. Reported once per film with the distinct values.

fill.description: APPLIED. The variant for card/tiles/pills/answer, defaulting from design.fills. A value outside the vocabulary, or on a type that has none, fails the build.

align.description: APPLIED. Cross-axis position of the element in the scene AND the text alignment of everything inside it — the descendant half matters, because .hss-text and .hss-stat-label set text-align themselves and would otherwise ignore a host-level setting.

group.description: APPLIED. Consecutive elements sharing a name go inside one row wrapper. It is a layout instruction, not an element type: each element keeps its own id and its own phase.

layout.description: APPLIED. `grid` is what a two-column "given | solving" solve needs; a wrapping flex row is not a grid, and `columns` on a row is reported rather than accepted and dropped.

columns.description: APPLIED. On a `tiles` element it is the tile grid. On anything else it is the group's column count and requires layout: "grid".

radius.description: APPLIED — border-radius on the element host.

max_width.description: APPLIED — the measure cap. Defaults from design.text_width[role].

gap.description: APPLIED — gap on the element host, inherited by its row/group wrapper.

panel.description: APPLIED for card/tiles — a per-element surface override.

slab_bg.description: APPLIED. The brutalist name slab: display type reversed out of a solid brand block. NOT `label_bg` — that was the typo that shipped, and this schema is why it cannot ship again.

slab_ink.description: APPLIED. The type ON a slab. A different role from the stage ink; sharing one is how a bright block ends up paper-on-yellow at 1.43:1.

meter.description: APPLIED for card. The meter runs on its OWN phase so a panel can settle while its bar is still filling. Width is a function of t, never a CSS transition — a transition reads the wall clock and breaks determinism.

meter_at_ms.description: APPLIED — the meter phase offset from the element's own at_ms.

place.description: DISCARDED for credit — the emitter pins a credit to bottom-centre, so an authored place is reported. Kept so the intent stays in the record.

shape.description: APPLIED for shape — the mark. `box` and `underline` are CSS borders (the two legacy kinds); `dbl-underline` is the double rule that draws itself under the target; `circle` rings its target with a stroke that draws on; `arrow` is a fixed-size curved pointer coming from `side`; `highlight` is a marker swipe wiped left to right. Every kind requires `of`. The emitter's own vocabulary is the contract — an unknown kind defers the element with the emitter's message, and this enum is the authoring-side convenience, exactly like `type`.

side.description: APPLIED for shape (arrow only) — which edge the arrow comes from, default `left`. left/right reach across the scene's side margins, top/bottom across the gap above and below; on any other kind it is reported and dropped.

of.description: APPLIED for shape — the id of the element this mark annotates. Required for every kind: the mark's wrapper is moved into the target's own box at setup and positioned around it, so a shape with no target is a mark that draws nothing, which reel-compile reports rather than renders.

width.description: DISCARDED. The stage is a flow layout; there is no width to set. Use max_width.

rotate.description: DISCARDED. The runtime OWNS `transform` on every frame — _ap writes scale()/translate() — so any authored angle would be overwritten sixty times a second. It needs a composite, not a declaration.

ambient.description: DISCARDED in full — there is no decorative-layer concept. Reported per scene with a count, so the loss is visible without being a build failure.

start.description: APPLIED when it equals the timeline chain. OPTIONAL: when omitted the scene starts where the previous scene ends (0 for the first). Durations are the source of truth — when an authored start disagrees with the chain, the chain wins and the disagreement is reported, so retiming one scene reflows every later scene instead of demanding hand-computed starts.

dur.description: APPLIED — seconds. OPTIONAL: defaults to 3, short enough that a new scene is engaging by default and long enough for one idea.

tone.description: DISCARDED as a colour source: it resolved nothing the compiler could read. It is still accepted and reported; use `color` per element instead.

frame.description: DISCARDED — a narrative label for the beat, not layout.

exit.description: DISCARDED — the emitter cross-fades scenes on a fixed curve.

gap.description: APPLIED — the scene's flex column gap.

duration.description: SECONDS, not ms. The whole reason reel-compile.cjs exists: the IR uses seconds and the emitter uses ms, and feeding one to the other silently yields dur=NaN — a clip with no length. OPTIONAL: when omitted the scene chain decides — the clip is exactly as long as its scenes. When present it is checked against the chain; a disagreement is reported and the chain wins, same rule as scene.start.

design.description: DISCARDED — a free-text design statement, kept for the record.

source_mock.description: DISCARDED — where the mock came from.

tokens.description: LEGACY — the pre-`design` palette, used by breath-of-air which predates the design block. Superseded by design.tokens.

x_summary.description: Author's own tally, kept so the storyboard can be read without running the compiler. It is named like an annotation and is one, but it is structured rather than free text — which is why the root's `x_` pattern carves out `summary` instead of claiming it and then failing the object below.
